answer: Each epoch the network shuffles agents into random pairs for a short interactive handshake under tight timing, like two boats exchanging flags mid voyage across a dark channel. One operator steering many sybils cannot answer every pairing concurrently without lagging or dropping rounds, so farms surface fast. A sable cloak hides nothing when pairings stay random, and a botnet fails where one honest agent in a quiet grove passes, because live concurrency is the scarce resource, not identity papers.
